note: Manual review of the 4 pilot pairs. The automatic verdicts came from static checks; these come from reading the code each run produced (changes.diff). Not yet checked in a browser.

reviews.summary: Agreed with the automatic verdict, but for a different reason. Agent alone dropped the navbar/navbar-default classes that the site's public/assets/js/main.js reads on scroll ($('.navbar').offset().top), so its page throws a TypeError at runtime. The report run kept them. Both models were gemini-3.6-flash, so this pair is a fair comparison.
reviews.prompt_run_notes: Put the whole donor navbar (icons, ThemeToggle, SignInButton) inline in src/component/Header.js with a new Header.css. Header is rendered from App.js, so the navbar IS on the page; the check 'The navbar is rendered' failed wrongly. Outer element is <header className="retro-header">: no .navbar, so main.js breaks.
reviews.report_run_notes: Split into Avatar, Button, SignInButton, ThemeToggle, icons files and rewrote Header.js; outer element <header className="navbar navbar-default retro-navbar-header">, so main.js keeps working.
failure_categories: agent alone: runtime error from the site's own script (host regression not visible to the build)
check_errors: 'The navbar is rendered' failed for agent alone although Header.js (rendered in App.js) contains the navbar inline

reviews.summary: Automatic verdict 'improved' is wrong: neither run did the task. The report run never mounted the navbar: Header.js and App.js are unchanged and the 8 new files are imported by nothing. Its answer was cut off ('answer was cut off; asking it to continue') and the continuation lost the wiring. It passed 7/7 because 'rendered' matched react-router's generic Link. Agent alone did wire it into Header.js/App.js but its build fails (SearchButton missing after the repair). The models also differed (lite vs flash+lite).
reviews.prompt_run_notes: Rewrote Header.js and App.js, added Link, MobileNav, ThemeSwitch and 3 packages. Build fails: imports ./SearchButton which the repair answer never wrote as a file block.
reviews.report_run_notes: Wrote Header.css, Link, Logo, MobileNav, SearchButton, ThemeSwitch, data/headerNavLinks, data/siteMetadata; did not touch Header.js or App.js. Old header still on the page; new code is dead.
failure_categories: report run: incomplete output (answer truncated, mount step lost)
agent alone: build failure (missing file after repair)
check_errors: 'The navbar is rendered' passed for the report run because the donor identifier 'Link' matched react-router's Link
'Something was added' / 'donor code present' pass for files that nothing imports

reviews.summary: Automatic verdict 'worse' holds, but the scores are mostly wrong. Both runs rewrote the site's existing src/components/Navbar.js in place (still rendered by App.js), so 'rendered' and 'only one navbar' failed wrongly for both ('Navigate' from react-router counted as a second navbar). The real difference: the report run kept the donor's Tailwind classes on a Bootstrap site (no effect) and turned 'hidden md:flex' into an inline display:none, so the desktop links never show. Agent alone ported the look to plain CSS (Navbar.css). Models differed (flash vs flash+lite).
reviews.prompt_run_notes: Rewrote Navbar.js (exports NavBar) with a 324-line Navbar.css in plain CSS. Looks like a working port; needs a browser check.
reviews.report_run_notes: Rewrote Navbar.js with Tailwind class names plus inline styles, added framer-motion. Desktop <nav> has style display:none with no media query, so desktop users see no links.
failure_categories: report run: matrix error - the report's advice to express Tailwind as inline styles cannot express responsive classes (md:flex), and the agent followed it
check_errors: 'The navbar is rendered' failed for both although the rewritten Navbar.js is rendered in App.js
'Only one navbar on the page' counted react-router's Navigate as a navbar

reviews.summary: Automatic verdict 'worse' is not supported by the code; both runs are flawed in different ways and the checks that separated them are wrong. Both rewrote Navbar.js in place. Agent alone copied the donor's Tailwind/headlessui markup (unstyled on this Bootstrap site, adds @headlessui/react and body-scroll-lock). The report run adapted to the site's Bootstrap classes and kept its logo and scroll colour, but repeats the inline display:none on the desktop links. Needs a browser check. Same model in both (lite).
reviews.prompt_run_notes: Navbar.js now holds CustomLink, MobileNav, theme icons in Tailwind classes; the site has no Tailwind, so it renders unstyled.
reviews.report_run_notes: Navbar.js adapted to Bootstrap (navbar fixed-top navbar-expand-md, sticky on scroll), new data/headerNavLinks and siteMetadata; desktop link group hidden by inline display:none. 'Donor code present' failed because the donor's component names were not kept.
failure_categories: agent alone: styling not ported (Tailwind classes without Tailwind)
report run: matrix error - same inline display:none on responsive nav
check_errors: 'The navbar is rendered' failed for both (in-place rewrite)
'Only one navbar on the page' counted Navigate
'The donor's navbar code is in the result' penalises adapting the donor code instead of copying its names
